jobs.occupation: Biologe (m/w/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Every year, 225.000 patients are treated in 30 clinics, 27 institutes and specialized centers. The over 8.000 employees offer medical care with state-of-the-art diagnosis and therapies, which meet highest international standards. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral antivity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.At the Insitute of Medical Microbiology (working group of PD Dr. Torben Knuschke), we are therefore offering the following position, which is fully funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and will start on 1 January 2027Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) funtions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cellsApply molecular biology techniquesPlan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studiesPresent research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publicationsAssist in supervising Bachelors/Masters studentsA completed Master´s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related fieldSolid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniquesExperience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantageStrong interest in basic research in Virology/ImmunologyIndependent, structured, and team-oriented working-styleExcellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredAn exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research fieldDedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminarsState-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital EssenInterdisciplinary work with colleagues from other departmentsEnrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Sciences BIOME (https://www.uni-due.de/biome)Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 yearsA collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideasFamily-friendly corporate culture

jobs.description: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. jobs.description: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The research group Plankton Imaging Technology and Deep-Sea Zooplankton Ecology at GEOMAR (in cooperation with Kiel University’s Marine Data Science Group) is offering a position in the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” starting at the earliest possible date.The position is offered for a duration of 3 years, with the possibility of extension. In the first year, the successful candidate will be employed by GEOMAR at 75%, supplemented by a 25% contract at Kiel University. Years two and three are fully funded at 100% (pay grade E13 according to the collective agreement for the public sector, TVöD, depending on experience).The position offers the opportunity to pursue a doctoral degree in natural or computer science as a member of the “Helmholtz School for Marine Data Science” (MarDATA). MarDATA’s interdisciplinary focus spans supercomputing, modeling, (bio)informatics, robotics, statistics, and big data methodologies. Doctoral researchers benefit from a structured training program that promotes cross-disciplinary collaboration and provides in-depth scientific insight as well as a systematic approach to marine data science. For more information, visit: https://www.mardata.de/. As part of the MarDATA doctoral network, the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” aims at exploring the use of underwater light field cameras for observing and characterizing plankton organisms (zooplankton) in the ocean. Light field cameras deviate from off-the-shelf cameras in that all rays have to pass through an extra microlens array that changes their direction.
